**2026-11-03.** A patch release that repairs the public nightly test run. The nightly was red because a test fixture never reached the public tree. The engine's source code is unchanged from 0.6.15; the only change to what ships is one dependency bump in the lockfile, below. There is no `urn:sutra:q:1.0` change, no archive format, deploymentId or snapshot format change, and no migration.

## Fixed

- **The nightly tier-2 run had failed since 0.6.10 because a fixture was missing from the public
  tree.** Three `tc_store_features` tests failed while assembling their package, with
  `SUTRA.DEPLOY.MIGRATIONS.LAYOUT_INVALID`, because
  `rust/crates/sutra-conformance/fixtures/store-features/default--storefeat--1.0.0/migrations/results/V001__data_store.sql`
  was not there. The public export excluded every folder named `results` at any depth, when it only
  meant load-test and bench output, and the tree comparison used to check the export skipped the
  same name, so it reported the two trees in sync. Only this test fixture was affected: no engine
  code, published image or binary was missing anything.
- **The excludes now name the real output folders**, `rust/bench/results/` and
  `tools/sutra-load-test/results/`. A folder called `results` anywhere else is exported. The two
  tracked placeholders in those output folders, a `.gitignore` and a `.gitkeep`, were dropped the
  same way and are now in the public tree too.
- **A silent drop now fails the export.** Every file tracked in the exported trees must reach the
  public tree and must not be ignored there, except for a short documented list of export tooling.

## Changed

- `async-executor` moves from 1.14.0 to 1.14.1 in `rust/Cargo.lock`. Version 1.14.0 was yanked from
  crates.io after 0.6.15, which made `cargo deny check` fail. It reaches the engine through the
  RabbitMQ transport's client library.
- `.trivyignore.yaml` gains three time-boxed entries for new libstdc++ advisories (CVE-2026-114690,
  CVE-2026-114691, CVE-2026-115455) reported against the image's base packages. Debian ships no fix, and
  the engine does not link libstdc++.

## Known issue

- `tc_outbox_relay_recovers_from_a_postgres_crash_mid_flight` can still fail intermittently, so a
  nightly run can still go red on it. This release does not fix it. When PostgreSQL dies mid-flight,
  an inbound hop's duplicate check can fail on the dying connection. That check fails open: the hop
  is processed, and no dedup record is written for it. The test then finds one record fewer than
  settled orders (`every hop recorded (1498 < 1499)`). In these failures every accepted order still
  called back. A redelivery of such a hop would not be recognised as a duplicate.
